questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was a mix between academic and exploring something new. 

Nothing specific was important to me, I think I would be happy wherever. For me going to Prague was great because it is a city rich of culture and history

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My stay was great because I made it great, but if I look at it critically, there was a bunch of administrative troubles with Charles University.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University didnt offer any hotlines or anything we could contact

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Charles University's Erasmus hours were limited (only a couple of hours at school)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was one orientation day and it was a lot of information that was not too important

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend finding housing very early as in 6 months prior at a minimum (you can use Student Room Flat or so on), in that way you can find cheaper opions. 
Facebook is definitaly cheapest. 
there are a bunch of facebook groups, this is an example: Praha - Bydlení v Praze, Spolubydlení, nájem, pronájem, podnájem, byt, dům

watch out for scammers!!

I got a room from "Erasmus in Prague (Sokolská)" it was a crazy noisy road I was living on and it was quite pricy for the Prague standard (16000czk-4900dkr)
I found my room through Facebook but it was an Erasmus in Prague Apartment.

Dorms are reaaaly cheap (1200 dkr ca) but nasty. All my friends were complaining.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really easy to make friends if you live in the dorms, so if you don't feel comfortable being independent and finding friends yourself, you should consider it. CU science did not have any activities to get to know your fellow students, we only had an orientation day where I randomly made my friends for the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Dorms are cheap but far away from the city, and not very clean. Some of my friends had issues with cockroaches

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration for science was easy, the course you applied for from back home were the ones you got.
But if you want courses from social sceince faculty it is a complete mess. In my case their registration opened up prior to us even getting our log-in information. Registration is also first come first serve (først til mølle) which does not make any sense if you want courses from outside your faculty. I was very unsatisfied by that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could send a mail or visit the office to you erasmus coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 50% succesful. I got all my geography courses but not my social science courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read up on the rules. You can change faculty, if you want to do more courses in social science, ask the erasmus coordinator in Copenhagen to be admitted there and so on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was so and so. It was a little similar to danish high school and mostly very easy to pass and complete

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: higher workload throughout the course, but exams were very easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the teachers were very passionate and great, some of them were very a little too affected of growing up in communism.

Energy Security in Israel and the Middle East - JPM822
very interesting especially in the context of israel-gaza conflict, my lecturer were Israeli. Also easy to finish (4 day intensive course and a 2000 word easy)

special topics in Poli1cal Geography - MZ340V10
This one was also super interesting. There were guest lecturers every week introducting their geopolitical articles.

the teacher in this course were not very nice. She would publicly "shame" students who scored low on tests

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use the first weekends to go travel around, before you know it the months have passed by.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I unfortunately did not have any contact with the locals. All my courses were only Erasmus student

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would not know unfortunately.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Czech people in service can be rude, but other than that I thought they were nice people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The city and its history

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- open up, do not only talk to danish student but mingle with the internationals
- do as much as possible
- push yourself

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
- Read these evaluations
- ask questions

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
- meeting a bunch of internationals
- getting a lot of friends
- living in a new country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: - not knowing the local language in a country you live in was very unique

questions.answer: Yes
